I don't use TikTok myself, but from second-hand reports, the platform seems to have become a massive database of terrible advice. Recently, there are even tutorial videos telling people to put their iPhones in the fridge to cool them down…

Engadget cited one such example.

Of course, you should never do this. The most likely outcome is that condensation will form on the phone's internal components, whether while it's in the fridge or after you take it out. There's also a risk of thermal shock, to which lithium batteries are particularly sensitive.

Over the past few weeks, the UK has been hit by a heatwave (by UK standards, of course), and reports indicate that phone repair shops have seen a marked increase in cases of damage caused by customers following this kind of advice.

Apple's official recommendation is that if your iPhone overheats, you should place it in a cool environment and let it cool down naturally. However, you should not leave it in a car. Even inside a car's glove compartment, temperatures on a hot day can be high enough to cause damage, and even lead to the battery catching fire.
